name: Separate decision routing from prose generation
summary: Use a bounded decision layer before a stronger writing model.
steps: Submit the message and policy to the decision layer.
Interpret the returned disposition.
Invoke the writer only for dispositions requiring prose.
jarvis_use: Route routine inbox work before spending a full reasoning or writing call.

name: File messages without generating a reply
summary: Treat filing as an action rather than a writing task.
steps: Classify the message under the support policy.
If the result is Filed, save that result.
Skip the writer call.
jarvis_use: Archive informational notifications without manufacturing unnecessary responses.

name: Convert urgent support messages into prioritized follow-up
summary: Create an internal task directly from a routing decision.
steps: Evaluate whether the message requires follow-up.
Assign priority according to policy.
Save the internal task without drafting unless separately required.
jarvis_use: Turn an urgent operational issue into a P1 task rather than an unsolicited email.

name: Escalate review dispositions separately
summary: Preserve a review outcome instead of forcing every message into an automatic action.
steps: Allow a Needs review disposition.
Store the message in the review group.
Leave final resolution to a subsequent review process.
jarvis_use: Maintain a human-review queue for ambiguous or unsupported requests.

name: Draft replies only after a draft disposition
summary: Let the decision model select the branch and the writer compose the response.
steps: Obtain a Draft reply decision.
Pass the message and applicable business policy to the writer.
Save the generated draft separately from the routing result.
jarvis_use: Reserve the stronger model for substantive customer-facing composition.

name: Supply business policy and a test inbox explicitly
summary: Ground routing and writing in a fixed policy and known examples.
steps: Write the business rules separately from UI construction.
Prepare the test inbox.
Use the same policy and inputs in both architectures.
jarvis_use: Evaluate against Evens's actual task and communication rules rather than implicit model assumptions.

name: Keep the benchmark non-sending
summary: Test dispositions and drafts without contacting customers.
steps: Use a controlled inbox.
Save simulated actions and drafts.
Do not send customer messages or make account changes during comparison.
jarvis_use: Run safe Mac-operator experiments before permitting external actions.

name: Build a paired two-lane comparison
summary: Compare an all-writer baseline with a router-plus-writer architecture on the same inputs.
steps: Create an Opus-only lane.
Create a Jev-plus-Opus lane.
Feed each lane the same test messages.
Display outputs and measurements side by side.
jarvis_use: Measure whether adding a router improves the existing assistant rather than assuming it does.

name: Control writer model and effort across lanes
summary: Avoid attributing configuration differences to routing.
steps: Use the same writer model in both lanes.
Use the same effort setting.
Keep these settings fixed while comparing architectures.
jarvis_use: Make routing experiments comparable to the current Mac assistant baseline.

name: Start with a single non-writing case
summary: Isolate decision-path behavior before testing a mixed workload.
steps: Choose a message that should create a task rather than a reply.
Compare the resulting disposition and priority.
Check whether the combined lane avoided the writer.
jarvis_use: Smoke-test the fast path with one unambiguous internal-action request.

name: Stress-test with a mixed message batch
summary: Evaluate the architecture on messages requiring different kinds of work.
steps: Prepare a batch containing filing, follow-up, draft, and review cases.
Run both lanes on the same batch.
Compare outcomes, elapsed time, and writer calls.
jarvis_use: Check whether a router helps Evens's real workload mix.

name: Compare outcomes against expected dispositions
summary: Check correctness alongside speed.
steps: Associate test messages with expected outcomes.
Display each lane's outcome.
Mark whether each outcome matches the expectation.
jarvis_use: Prevent a faster but incorrect router from appearing successful.

name: Inspect per-message stage traces
summary: Expose who decided, who wrote, and what action was saved.
steps: Open a message's detail view.
Inspect decision and writing stages separately.
Compare stage durations and saved outcomes between lanes.
jarvis_use: Diagnose whether delay came from routing, drafting, or action handling.

name: Track completed messages, elapsed time, and writer calls
summary: Use more than one metric to assess routing benefit.
steps: Count completed messages.
Measure elapsed run time.
Count expensive writer invocations.
Display the metrics together.
jarvis_use: Make latency and model-use tradeoffs visible in the operator dashboard.

name: Interpret speed through workload composition
summary: Separate fast routing benefit from unavoidable writing time.
steps: Identify which messages require drafts.
Inspect drafting duration separately from decision duration.
Explain total performance in terms of the reply share.
jarvis_use: Choose routing targets with many non-writing tasks instead of expecting universal acceleration.

name: Rerun the test prompt after major changes
summary: Treat architecture edits as possible routing regressions.
steps: Keep a reusable test prompt and fixture.
Run it after a significant change.
Check that the fast lane has not started sending every message to Opus.
jarvis_use: Add a routing regression check to assistant upgrades.

name: Expose Jev through a Zapier MCP server
summary: Make the decision service available through the client's managed tool bridge.
steps: Prepare the client-specific MCP server.
Configure the TypeSafe Jev connection.
Expose the intended Jev action to that server.
Connect the consuming client.
jarvis_use: Use an existing MCP integration surface instead of inventing an unseen direct API path.

name: Provision only intended managed actions
summary: Treat a newly created managed server as empty until actions are explicitly added.
steps: Inspect the server's available tools.
If only get_configuration is exposed, add the required action.
Verify that the intended client can discover it.
jarvis_use: Keep each assistant limited to explicitly provisioned capabilities.

name: Keep provider and MCP credentials in separate homes
summary: Do not interchange the TypeSafe API key and the MCP connection credential.
steps: Store the TypeSafe key in the TypeSafe Jev connection.
Store the MCP credential in the application's MCP configuration.
Check credential placement when OAuth authentication fails.
jarvis_use: Avoid authentication failures while keeping secrets out of shared research artifacts.

name: Validate structured output types at the tool boundary
summary: Ensure confidence and other fields satisfy the managed action's actual schema.
steps: Inspect the required field types.
Serialize confidence as the required numeric type rather than text.
Check for tool rejection before accepting the integration as healthy.
jarvis_use: Catch schema errors before they silently disable the fast path.

name: Inspect the error behind every fallback
summary: A successful final answer does not prove the router worked.
steps: Detect when the request falls back to the writer.
Inspect the underlying tool error.
Fix the routing failure.
Verify that writer-call counts decrease on eligible cases.
jarvis_use: Prevent smooth fallback from masking a permanently broken decision layer.

name: Keep classifier output distinct from explanatory prose
summary: Do not attribute generated explanations to a model that returned only labels and confidence.
steps: Retain the actual structured result.
Display the labels and confidence as returned.
Label any application-written explanation separately.
jarvis_use: Maintain trustworthy decision provenance in the assistant's activity feed.

name: Match managed-tool wiring to the configured server
summary: Adapt integration prompts to the real server rather than assuming tool names and operations.
steps: Substitute the actual MCP server used by the application.
Inspect its exposed managed tools.
Align the integration with those tool names and operations.
jarvis_use: Keep the Mac operator grounded in the current tool inventory.

name: Separate assistant-specific MCP server inventories
summary: Maintain distinct configured servers for different assistant contexts.
steps: Create a server for the Claude context.
Create a separate server for the Jarvis context.
Configure each app inventory for its intended consumer.
jarvis_use: Avoid giving every assistant the same unnecessarily broad tool set.

name: Verify the client's displayed connector state
summary: Inspect connection status in the actual client rather than assuming setup completed.
steps: Inspect the client's connector configuration.
Check the Zapier connection's displayed state.
Treat Connected as a connection check, not proof of a successful action.
jarvis_use: Perform a grounded connection preflight before attempting tool work.

name: Build the application through staged coding prompts
summary: Separate foundation, policy/input setup, presentation, and testing prompts.
steps: Start with the two-lane foundation prompt.
Add the policy and test inbox.
Configure the tool connection.
Apply the dashboard presentation prompt.
Run the testing prompt.
jarvis_use: Turn a large assistant build into reviewable stages instead of one opaque instruction.

name: Polish the dashboard after establishing behavior
summary: Use a separate product-style presentation pass.
steps: Build the functional comparison first.
Apply the separate dashboard prompt.
Preserve visible metrics and inspectable outcomes while improving presentation.
jarvis_use: Improve operator readability without conflating visual polish with functional correctness.

name: Install a versioned local assistant package with a coding agent
summary: Use a downloaded release package as the installation input.
steps: Download the versioned Jarvis ZIP.
Leave it in Downloads as instructed.
Ask Claude Code to install that package.
Check the resulting local application.
jarvis_use: Adapt the package-based installation pattern after reviewing the package's trustworthiness.

name: Upgrade while preserving assistant state
summary: Make preservation of existing brain, notes, and settings an explicit upgrade requirement.
steps: Identify the existing installation.
Request an upgrade from the versioned package.
Explicitly require preservation of brain, notes, and settings.
Verify preservation after the upgrade.
jarvis_use: Avoid treating an assistant upgrade as permission to replace Evens's accumulated state.

name: Place an optional reflex layer before the main assistant
summary: Use a small decision service for rapid control decisions before deeper processing.
steps: Configure the optional TypeSafe key for reflex use.
Run narrowly scoped decisions before the main reasoning path.
Use the decision to control whether subsequent processing proceeds.
jarvis_use: Prototype a bounded control layer without replacing the main assistant model.

name: Classify whether an utterance contains a question
summary: The Jarvis course advertises a reflex decision about whether the user asked a question.
steps: Provide the current utterance to the reflex layer.
Obtain a question-present decision.
Use that result as an input to the response policy.
jarvis_use: Test whether a lightweight question detector reduces unnecessary full-model turns.

name: Classify end of speaking before responding
summary: The advertised reflex layer decides whether the user has finished the sentence.
steps: Evaluate the current speech context.
Decide whether the turn appears complete.
Delay or permit the next response stage accordingly.
jarvis_use: Explore less interruptive voice interaction in a sandbox before live deployment.

name: Gate processing on listening state
summary: The advertised reflex layer distinguishes speaking while the assistant is listening from other states.
steps: Provide the relevant listening/session state.
Obtain the reflex decision.
Use it to decide whether the main assistant should act on the utterance.
jarvis_use: Reduce accidental activation from speech outside an intended listening session.

name: Send selected note excerpts rather than the full store
summary: The course claims local selection of short note excerpts for reflex context.
steps: Keep the stored notes local.
Select only the excerpts needed for the current decision.
Send those excerpts to the external service.
Verify actual transmission before relying on the privacy claim.
jarvis_use: Apply context minimization and audit what leaves Evens's Mac.

name: Expose reflex activity in a local operator view
summary: Make the reflex layer inspectable rather than wholly invisible.
steps: Open the local assistant interface.
Expose reflex status or activity alongside the main assistant view.
Inspect decisions when testing the integration.
jarvis_use: Provide an operator-visible place to audit rapid routing decisions.

name: Retrieve reusable lesson resources from the classroom
summary: Use attached prompt-pack files as inspectable build inputs instead of relying only on a video.
steps: Locate the relevant classroom lesson.
Inspect its Resources area.
Obtain the attached PDF.
Confirm that the file matches the intended build before using it.
jarvis_use: Ingest the actual written build instructions while preserving uncertainty about which pack was attached.
